YOUR READING ROUTINE

Read and practise Hanzi.

  1. Try the Hanzi first. Read the whole conversation. Hover over a dialogue character for pinyin when you need it. Notice who, where, when, and why.
  2. Find words, not isolated guesses. Switch on word help only when stuck. Notice how characters join into words such as 电话 and 电脑.
  3. Practise the words. Use Match characters or Write words to practise recognition and handwriting on paper.

Why this approach?

Chinese reading involves recognising character forms, connecting them to words and meanings, and understanding the passage. This site combines those skills, with repeated reading and retrieval practice.

The reading routine is a practical design informed by research, not a validated teaching programme. Repeated-reading evidence in the Chinese study below comes from one heritage learner.

  • Chinese second-language reading: meta-analysis
  • Character recognition, word knowledge, and comprehension
  • Assisted repeated reading: Chinese case study

Coverage: all four main 课文 dialogues in each of the book’s 15 lessons. Warm-ups, grammar examples, and workbook exercises are outside this dialogue collection. Original wording is retained; spacing and punctuation are normalised.
